CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the effectiveness of ongoing treatment for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with emphasis on evaluating symptom control and any adverse effects since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, expressing mixed feelings regarding his overall progress. He reports that his anxiety levels have remained stable, but he continues to experience significant irritability, particularly during high-stress situations at work. He has adhered to his sertraline regimen of 300 mg daily without any reported side effects; however, he notes that his concentration issues have persisted, especially during critical meetings, which he finds increasingly frustrating.
Mr. Smith's tension-type headaches have remained consistent, occurring approximately once a week with an intensity ranging from 3 to 5 out of 10. He continues to find topiramate at 150 mg daily effective, and he has maintained his ibuprofen usage at a frequency of once a month for occasional breakthrough headaches. Sleep quality remains improved, with Mr. Smith averaging 7 to 8 hours of sleep per night, thanks to the combination of trazodone and melatonin. Nonetheless, he reports that morning grogginess has not resolved and is becoming a concern for him.
Despite the improvements in sleep and headache control, Mr. Smith describes ongoing fatigue, particularly in the afternoons, which he attributes to his demanding work schedule. He is eager to discuss additional strategies to enhance his energy levels and overall productivity, as he feels that fatigue is impacting his performance at work.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (reduced frequency) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (discontinued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to maintain a healthy lifestyle, engaging in regular physical activity, including brisk walking and weekend hiking. He has further reduced his caffeine intake and follows a balanced diet, which he believes has positively impacted his anxiety levels. His mindfulness practices, including meditation and yoga, remain integral to his daily routine, and he continues to journal, which aids in emotional processing and self-reflection.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; persistent irritability noted; sleep quality improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue reported, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.7F - General: Alert, oriented; appears mildly fatigued but engaged; mood appears anxious with moderate distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with moderate distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Recommend ongoing cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to further address irritability and concentration challenges. Discuss potential referrals for stress management techniques if symptoms persist. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime and melatonin 3 mg nightly; reassess efficacy and side effects in one month. Monitor for any changes in sleep architecture. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain headache diary to monitor frequency and intensity. Reassess in one month and consider referral to a neurologist if headaches worsen or if new symptoms develop. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued lifestyle modifications, including regular physical activity and dietary adjustments. Discuss the potential for introducing a stimulant medication, such as modafinil, to help manage fatigue, pending further evaluation of sleep quality. Consider referral to a sleep specialist for further evaluation of potential underlying conditions, including sleep apnea or thyroid dysfunction. Recommend stress management techniques to enhance energy levels.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-05-23 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
